title: Halfway across the bridge

hosts.Leyla: lives in Baku and loves a good plan
hosts.Sam: grew up in Manchester and once travelled with no plan at all

before.predict: What are you afraid of? Guess: who in this episode is scared of heights — Leyla or Sam?

chapters.title: The glass bridge
chapters.prompt: CHAPTER 1 SCENE: a glass bridge high between green mountains, a woman with long dark hair and a lavender jacket frozen in the middle holding the rail with both hands, eyes shut, a friend gently holding her other hand, tiny trees far below

chapters.title: A speech at a wedding
chapters.prompt: CHAPTER 2 SCENE: a wedding reception, a red-haired bearded man in a suit standing with a microphone and a sheet of paper, nervous but smiling, guests at round tables laughing warmly, fairy lights

chapters.title: Step by step
chapters.prompt: CHAPTER 3 SCENE: a staircase of soft clouds going up into a warm sunrise, small footprints on each step, a little flag at the top, calm and hopeful, no people

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is fears and phobias. And Leyla, I know your secret.
[sigh] Yes, everyone knows. I'm scared of heights. It's a real phobia.
Tell them about the glass bridge.
Last spring, in the mountains, my friends wanted to walk across a glass bridge. I looked down and I was scared stiff. I could not move.
What did your friends do?
One friend held my hand and tried to reassure me. "It's safe, Leyla. Thousands of people walk here every day."
Did it help?
Not really. I know the fear is irrational. The bridge is strong. But my body doesn't listen.
I understand. My trigger is different. Put me in front of a big audience, and my hands start shaking.
Public speaking?
Yes. At my best friend's wedding, I had to give a speech. The night before, I started to get cold feet. I wanted to call him and say, "Ask someone else."
But you didn't.
No. Everyone says: face your fears. So I did. I practised the speech twenty times in front of my cat.
[laugh] And on the day?
My voice was shaking for the first minute. Then people laughed at my first joke, and the anxiety just… went away.
That's a great way to overcome a fear — step by step.
And you? Did you cross the bridge in the end?
Half of it. Then I had a small panic attack and walked back. But next year I will try again.
Half is good! And at least it's not a nightmare any more.
Here's your question for your next SpeakLab call: what are you afraid of — and have you ever tried to face it?
Mine is spiders. But let's not talk about that. See you next time!
Bye for now!

options: Fears and how to deal with them
questions.why: Leyla's fear of heights, Sam's fear of speaking in public, and facing them.

questions.q: What happened to Leyla on the glass bridge?
options: She crossed half of it and walked back
She refused to go near it
She took photos from the middle

questions.why: "I practised the speech twenty times in front of my cat."

questions.q: Sam asked someone else to give the speech.
questions.why: He wanted to, but he did not — he gave the speech.
